Edit: This would have no impact on insurances purchased by other's, that is correct but immaterial as we are discussing insurance that he presumably was the controller of.

The insurance policy is a contract where the insurer promises to give something of value to the beneficiary when an insured event occurs. At no time is the thing of value owned by the policy holder or their estate, unless they are a beneficiary.

This is important because life insurance pays out to the beneficiaries the moment the insurance company verifies the death. A hotly contested will might take decades to work its way through the probate court, but life insurance generally pays the beneficiaries within days. This is why even wealthy people buy life insurance: instant support for the survivors.

Some insurance policies have a "cash value" feature, but this is not insurance. It is a savings account or annuity described by the same contract as the actual insurance. The "cash value" feature does indeed become part of the estate upon death.
